description.narrative:
Afrobarometer is an African organization that conducts research and surveys of public opinion of ordinary Africans regarding issues of democracy, human rights, and other topics. It started in 1999 and Sida has supported them from the start.
The partnerAfrobarometer (AB) submitted, 29 July 2022, a funding propsal for core support for the five year period 2023-2027 and requesting 160 MSEK from Sida for the whole period (78% increase compared to current levels of Sida funding; see more under budget). A revised proposal was submitted 17 August 2022. Afrobarometer has been a cooperation partner to Sida ever since it was established in 1999 (although AB was only established as its own legal entity in 2019; before that it was housed under the organization CDD-Ghana with which Sida entered into agreement with before AB's establishment in 2019). AB is a non-profit entity headquartered in Ghana. It is a pan-African survey research network that conducts public attitude surveys on democracy, governance, the economy, and society. 39 countries have been surveyed since its start in 1999. The network encompasses more than 30 national partners responsible for data collection, analysis, and in-country dissemination of findings. Regional coordination is provided by the Ghana Center for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana), the Institute for Justice and Reconciliation (IJR) in South Africa, and the Institute for Development Studies (IDS) at the University of Nairobi in Kenya. Michigan State University (MSU) and the University of Cape Town (UCT) provide technical support to the network. Important donors, other than Sida, are USAID, USIP, Mo Ibrahim Foundation, OSF, Gates Foundation, Mastercard, WB, GIZ and more. The interventionAB is seeking core support from Sida and the current aid modality has been a hybrid core/project support, with non-earmarked funding, but with audit terms of reference normally used for project support, i.e. ISA 800/805 as well as ISRS 4400. Sida support will be non-earmarked and could contribute to all AB's work streams including staffing and adminstration. AB's work in the 2023-2027 period their proposal covers focus on rounds 10, 11 and part of 12 of its surveys. More specifically the period will include: i) field surveys in at least 40 African countries; ii) develop a credible phone survey methodology; iii) implement essential capacity-building programs; iv) develop, sustain and expand AB’s analytic and signature products; v) widely disseminate survey results with a focus on expanding our audiences and uptake; vi) continue and deepen outreach to the African Union and its allied bodies, sub-regional economic communities, as well as universities; and vii) collaborate with the media and identifiable civil society and advocacy groups, notably women, youth and minority groups to extend our reach and impact.Most recent evaluation of ABThe most recent evaluation that have been done on AB is an evaluation conducted by Niras (commissioned by Sida) and dated 30 Nov. 2021. The evaluation was a mid-term evaluation of AB's regional programme (2018-2022), focusing on relevance, effectiveness, efficiency and sustainability with a view to strengthen the remainder of the agreement phase as well as providing recommendations for a possible new phase. The evaluation contains 13 recommendations, including on monitoring and evaluation, regional and national partnership, youth engagement, local resource mobilization (focus on African sources), and diversify fundraising.

Afrobarometer är en afrikansk organisation som bedriver forskning och undersökningar av den allmänna opinionen hos vanliga afrikaner angående frågor om demokrati, mänskliga rättigheter och andra ämnen. Det startade 1999 och Sida har stöttat dem från starten.
PartnerAfrobarometer (AB) lämnade den 29 juli 2022 ett finansieringsförslag för kärnstöd för femårsperioden 2023-2027 och begärde 160 MSEK från Sida för hela perioden (78 % ökning jämfört med nuvarande nivåer av Sida-finansiering; se mer under budget). Ett reviderat förslag lämnades 17 augusti 2022. Afrobarometer har varit samarbetspartner till Sida ända sedan det bildades 1999 (även om AB bildades som egen juridisk person först 2019; dessförinnan var det inhyst under organisationen CDD-Ghana med som Sida ingick avtal med innan AB:s etablering 2019). AB är en ideell enhet med huvudkontor i Ghana. Det är ett panafrikanskt nätverk för undersökningar som genomför offentliga attitydundersökningar om demokrati, styrelseformer, ekonomi och samhälle. 39 länder har undersökts sedan starten 1999. Nätverket omfattar mer än 30 nationella partner som ansvarar för datainsamling, analys och spridning av resultat inom landet. Regional samordning tillhandahålls av Ghana Center for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana), Institutet för rättvisa och försoning (IJR) i Sydafrika och Institutet för utvecklingsstudier (IDS) vid University of Nairobi i Kenya. Michigan State University (MSU) och University of Cape Town (UCT) tillhandahåller tekniskt stöd till nätverket. Viktiga givare, förutom Sida, är USAID, USIP, Mo Ibrahim Foundation, OSF, Gates Foundation, Mastercard, WB, GIZ med flera. Insatsen AB söker kärnstöd från Sida och den nuvarande stödformen har varit en hybrid kärna/projektstöd, med icke öronmärkta medel, men med revisionsuppdrag som normalt används för projektstöd, det vill säga ISA 800/805 samt ISRS 4400 Sidas stöd kommer att vara icke-öronmärkt och kan bidra till alla AB:s arbetsflöden inklusive bemanning och administration. AB:s arbete under perioden 2023-2027 deras förslag omfattar fokus på omgångarna 10, 11 och en del av 12 av dess undersökningar. Mer specifikt kommer perioden att omfatta: i) fältundersökningar i minst 40 afrikanska länder; ii) utveckla en trovärdig metodik för telefonundersökningar; iii) genomföra viktiga kapacitetsuppbyggnadsprogram; iv) utveckla, upprätthålla och expandera AB:s analytiska och signaturprodukter; v) sprida undersökningsresultat i stor utsträckning med fokus på att utöka vår publik och spridning; vi) fortsätta och fördjupa räckvidden till Afrikanska unionen och dess allierade organ, subregionala ekonomiska gemenskaper, såväl som universitet; och vii) samarbeta med media och identifierbara civilsamhället och opinionsbildningsgrupper, särskilt kvinnor, ungdomar och minoritetsgrupper för att utöka vår räckvidd och genomslagskraft. Senaste utvärderingen av ABDen senaste utvärderingen som har gjorts av AB är en utvärdering utförd av Niras ( på uppdrag av Sida) och daterad 30 nov 2021. Utvärderingen var en halvtidsutvärdering av AB:s regionala program (2018-2022) med fokus på relevans, effektivitet, effektivitet och hållbarhet i syfte att stärka återstoden av avtalsfasen som samt ge rekommendationer för en eventuell ny fas. Utvärderingen innehåller 13 rekommendationer, inklusive om övervakning och utvärdering, regionalt och nationellt partnerskap, ungdomsengagemang, lokal resursmobilisering (fokus på afrikanska källor) och diversifierad insamling.

Objectives
Mission goal: To make citizen voice a key pillar of Africa policy and decision-making Impact goals:
1 Produce high-quality survey data and analysis on African attitudes, experiences and aspirations
2 Widely disseminate findings to Africa-related policy and development actors
3 Build capacity for survey research, analysis, and communication on the continent
Theory of Change
If African public opinion data are high-quality, independent, non-partisan, accessible, timely and relevant; and
If State-of-the-art research and analysis is produced; and
If A sustainable institution communicates effectively and builds survey research analysis, and communication capacity across the continent; and
If This work is led by, for, and with Africans;
Then Governments, policy makers and influencers and other stakeholders will use and value AB data and analysis; and
Therefore African citizens voices will be amplified and can better inform public policy and development decision-making for thriving societies.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sida and Afrobarometer 16094

description.narrative:
In 2024, the Afrobarometer continued to produce high-quality survey data and analysis by introducing new themes such as sexual and reproductive health, expanding coverage to countries like Chad, Comoros, and Guinea-Bissau, and including younger respondents aged 16 and 17. It managed the Data for Governance Alliance (D4GA), strengthening collaboration with the African Union and civil society organizations. National partners were supported through survey material reviews and fieldworker training. Additionally, datasets were cleaned and finalized for 28 countries for Round 9 during the reporting period, cross-round datasets were developed, and new templates for Round 10 dispatches were created.
Efforts to widely disseminate findings included hosting dissemination events in 21 of the 28 countries, with 9 completing all required deliverables. Numerous reports, papers, dispatches, and blog posts were released, and the organization participated in 83 global events to share data and insights.
To build capacity for survey research, analysis, and communication, six workshops were conducted in Kenya, Nigeria, and Senegal, training civil society organizations and journalists from 27 countries. Eight university programs across Africa reached 328 participants, and the inaugural workshop in South Africa selected 12 scholars from 10 countries. Sixteen fellowships were awarded, and French language training was launched. Progress was also made on developing a video training library and teaching toolkits.
In terms of data utility and policy visibility, several notable impacts were reported:
UNDPs 2023/2024 Human Development Report cited the organizations data to highlight African perceptions on taxing the rich, with most respondents indicating that current tax levels are "about the right amount."In Zimbabwe, UN Women referenced the data in a news article to underscore the prevalence of violence against women and girls, a major barrier to achieving gender equality (SDG 5).In Namibia in 2022, a paper emphasizing the urgency of addressing gender-based violence was produced by AB. This contributed to public discourse, including condemnation by former President Hage Geingob, and ultimately led to the passage of the Combating of Domestic Violence Amendment Bill.In Gambia, the 20232027 National Development Plan cited data on citizens views on democracy and corruption, helping shape the governments commitment to addressing gaps during the plans implementation.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
